diagnosis.scope: Posthoc descriptions of recorded support exchanges. Affine load scales bound static force requests at measured postures; they do not measure ground reaction, certify contact persistence or guarantee dynamic feasibility. Pre-guard envelopes include speed, slew and force caps; post-guard predictions and native actuator forces remain distinct. Prepared contact and posture observations delimit transfers. No counterfactual trajectories, causal isolation or new eligibility decisions.

interpretation: All four observed transfers remove the old primary force request and request its neutral joint position at entry. The replacement remains in contact for 5 to 14 controller intervals before contact loss and lost rotation.

All 68 replacement-joint transfer requests exceed their actuator force clamps. At entry, fixed-direction static load scaling under those clamps reaches only 38.3 to 54.5 percent of the request; the instantaneous pre-guard command envelope permits only 18.1 to 32.1 percent.
Replacement joint protection is inactive at all four entries; it affects 29 of 68 later/current transfer joint commands. The large initial mismatch is already present before that protection.

The 340 recorded replacement-joint actuator samples do not reach a force clamp within the stated tolerance. Requested torque exceeding a clamp is distinct from the observed actuator saturating: bounded target velocities, changing measured velocity and joint protection govern actual force.

The mean replacement-joint error is 8.204 N m before guards, 9.144 N m after guards, and 9.647 N m in retained native samples against the prepared request. These describe different quantities, not measured ground reaction or isolated causal effects.
This retained one-body diagnosis does not establish the result of gradual support sharing, validate alternate poses, qualify recovery, or alter the twelve-cohort 2704-failure outcome.
next_gate: Declare a distinct broad support-sharing successor that ranks replacement poses using their static torque-request bounds, retains original support while introducing the replacement force request, and stages unloading under measured contact and existing command protection. Compare multiple target and sharing variants across the exposed body cohort with fresh selected-reference and failed-exchange comparators. Keep nominal actuator limits, the five-degree reference-gain rule, complete applicable zero-world controls, full production-route coverage, retained-path screening and fresh full-capture varied-start confirmation. Static request bounds and contact presence do not establish load transfer or dynamic feasibility. Actual recovery is still required before the same-body Studio walk-fall-recover-resume handoff; startup and stepping performance remain separate product work.
